BaseTemplate.description: Starter code for your Nextjs Boilerplate with Tailwind CSS

Index.meta_description: Next js Boilerplate is the perfect starter code for your project. Build your React application with the Next.js framework.
Index.hero_title: Classroom quizzes, designed for the realtime era
Index.hero_description: Teachers create classes, quizzes and sessions in minutes; students answer question by question with autosave, TOTP checkpoints and detailed reports after class.
Index.hero_feature_1_desc: Import one <mono>questions.md</mono> file and your question bank is ready.
Index.hero_feature_2_desc: Students who lose connection keep their answers, which sync again once back online.
Index.hero_feature_3_desc: Students can only take the quiz when present in class, using a token at each round.
Index.feature_teacher_desc: Create classes, group students, map subjects – all in one dashboard. You always know which class you are teaching, which quiz you are using, and which students are participating.
Index.feature_bank_desc: Import Markdown/ZIP, add tags and split pools per chapter. Quiz rules automatically pick suitable questions for each test, no manual copy-paste needed.
Index.feature_screen_title: Project the QR, run TOTP checkpoints
Index.feature_screen_desc: Project the QR, students join from their phone/laptop. During the quiz, the system autosaves, blocks cheating with token checkpoints and lets teachers monitor in realtime.
Index.feature_reports_desc: After each session, review the scoreboard, token log and question distribution by tag. Use this data to refine your question bank and teaching strategy for the next semesters.
Index.use_cases_title: Designed for real classrooms, not just demos
Index.use_case_1_desc: Run quizzes for 100–200 students in one session, no paper tests needed.
Index.use_case_2_desc: Autosave + checkpoints help reduce cheating and the risk of losing answers.
Index.use_case_3_desc: Use BKquiz for a quick knowledge check-in after each class.
Index.free_open_source_desc: BKquiz is an open source project; you can self-host it or use the free cloud version.
Index.self_hosted_desc: Host on your own server, with full control of your data
Index.cloud_desc: Use it right away without setup, sign in with Google
Index.community_desc: BKquiz is an open source project, developed for the education community.
Index.github_desc: View the source code, contribute, or report issues
Index.license_desc: Apache License 2.0 - free to use, modify and distribute with patent protection
Index.contributing_desc: Contribute code, report bugs, or suggest new features
Index.faq_1_a: Yes, BKquiz is completely free and open source. You can use the free cloud version or self-host it on your own server.
Index.faq_2_a: Yes, BKquiz is open source and you can self-host it. See the setup guide in the GitHub repository. You only need Node.js, PostgreSQL and a few configuration steps to get it running.
Index.faq_3_a: If you self-host, you have full control of your data. The cloud version uses Google OAuth for authentication and follows security standards. Data is stored securely and only you have access to it.
Index.faq_4_q: Can I contribute to the project?
Index.faq_4_a: Very welcome! You can contribute code, report bugs, suggest features, or improve the documentation. See CONTRIBUTING.md on GitHub to learn how to contribute.
Index.faq_5_q: How many students does BKquiz support in one session?
Index.faq_5_a: BKquiz is designed to support large classes (100-200 students). If you self-host, the system can scale depending on your server configuration.

detail.scoring_hint_partial_halves: Each mistake (selecting a wrong option or missing a correct one) halves the score: 0 mistakes = 1, 1 = 0.5, 2 = 0.25, 3 or more = 0.
detail.scoring_hint_penalty: Selecting at least one correct option earns 1 point, minus {value} for each wrong option selected. The score never goes below 0.
